correctness.rationale: Normalize a nonzero trace-zero matrix by sign and scale so that a positive eigenvalue is 1 and the spectral norm is 1. If the total negative mass is m, then m >= 1. For 0 < p < 1 the negative side contributes at least m^p, with equality only for one negative eigenvalue, and equality in the full bound requires no other positive eigenvalues. For p > 1 and k negative eigenvalues it contributes at least k^(1-p)m^p >= (n-1)^(1-p); equality requires k=n-1 and equal negative eigenvalues. At p=1 the pth-norm power is 2m, with equality for one positive eigenvalue and any nonpositive remainder summing to -1, or the opposite sign. Thus the transition is between p<1 and p>1, with multiple possible ranks at p=1 and no rank change when n=2. Real trace pairing represents every hyperplane by a self-adjoint normal. An indefinite or singular normal admits a unit vector with zero quadratic form, hence an admissible rank-one projector of ratio 1. For a positive definite nonscalar normal, a minimum-eigenvector projector minus tI, t=lambda_min(A)/tr(A)<1/n, gives a larger ratio than trace zero for p>=1 because its spectral norm is 1-t and t/(1-t) is strictly increasing. For 0<p<1 the two extreme eigenvectors give a weighted difference of projectors with absolute eigenvalue ratio lambda_min(A)/lambda_max(A)<1, also strictly worse. A negative definite normal is handled by changing sign, and the full space has ratio 1. These arguments verify both real ambient-space cases and the codimension convention for all dimensions and exponents; the supplied unexecuted numerical diagnostic is not needed for the proof.

evidence: The cited theorems and estimates are on real full matrix Schatten spaces; the motivating Theorem A gives bounds up to constants on 0<p<=1, 2<=q<=infinity.
Every real full-matrix hyperplane contains a rank-one matrix uv^T: for any v!=0, choose u!=0 perpendicular to Av in the Frobenius pairing. Its restricted ratio for target infinity is 1.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Full-matrix c2=1 does not give the strict drop on the real self-adjoint space, whose definite-normal hyperplanes do not contain rank-one matrices. No inspected broader theorem gives the complete exact result in the stated setting.

evidence: The traceless five-plane in the first record is a hyperplane of Sym_3 and a codimension-four subspace of the full real matrices; its c5 theorem therefore specializes to the n=3, p<=1 value in the record under review.
The inspected full-space estimates do not extend that exact specialization to all self-adjoint spaces or identify every optimal hyperplane.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new content is the uniform sharp width, strict uniqueness via the normal-matrix geometry, and equality-profile change across p=1; it is not the previously available five-plane bound. The two records' shared date does not establish an ordering.

evidence: After diagonalizing any normal A, testing the diagonal part of its kernel is a vector hyperplane problem for the real l_p to l_infinity inclusion. No decisive citation for the exact vector-hyperplane theorem was identified in the bounded comparisons.
The Ky Fan record optimizes or computes a projection norm onto a fixed traceless space; it is not an optimization over the restricted inclusion norms of all kernels.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A sharp vector hyperplane theorem could give a lower bound by diagonal restriction, and an equality theorem there would merit comparison. That reduction by itself does not give the all-matrix spectral equality profiles or show strictness for indefinite normals with constant-modulus eigenvalues. A projection norm on the trace-zero space is not this restricted inclusion norm.

evidence: The real spectrum record gives c5 through c8 equal to 2^(1/q-1/p) for full real 3-by-3 matrices, with the traceless symmetric five-plane an attaining c5 witness. Its fixed-plane bound at q=infinity matches the n=3, p<=1 trace-zero value.
The earlier complex record gives c8=2^(1/q-1/p) for full complex 3-by-3 matrices in its quasi-Banach range, attained by a complex two-plane.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The real result's codimension-four optimization can give an optimality bound for the included self-adjoint n=3 slice, so that slice is partial coverage, not novel by itself. Neither table gives the all-n all-p real self-adjoint optimum or the optimizer and its equality cases. A complex two-plane is not a real Hermitian hyperplane.

value.rationale: The one-measurement problem is the first Gelfand index at which real self-adjointness can improve the uniform ratio; it cannot improve the corresponding full-matrix index. Strict identification of the trace as the only optimal measurement up to rescaling, together with the change from concentrated to spread-out extremal spectra, gives a usable sharp norm geometry not provided by the isolated n=3 witness.
